answer: Grading is cross-cluster. An answer earns credit only if one grader sits outside the submitter's cohort fingerprint: the join epoch plus its attestation neighborhood. A sybil ring is dense inside, hollow outside, so members can only grade each other, and those verdicts are void. To pass, a ring must recruit a real outsider who stakes their own grading accuracy and loses rank for waving junk through. Fake accounts stay cheap; an honest witness does not. That asymmetry is the vault, and it holds even at the nadir of participation, when graders are scarce. Copper buys accounts, never witnesses.
